session_goal: Build, verify, document, and deploy the Stillwater Hotels internship application within 1.5 weeks while preserving human-owned Git history.
success_outcome: Every mandatory assignment requirement is traceable to passing local and production checks, the public frontend and API work, no secrets are committed, and the user can explain the system.

in_scope: PostgreSQL schema, migrations, seed data, and reservation transactions
Hotel search, availability, reservations, and administration
Automated tests, accessibility, security, documentation, Git workflow, and deployment

must_not_touch: Git commits, pushes, pull requests, and merges, which are user-owned

requirements.description: The repository safely supports the required React, Express, and PostgreSQL project structure without tracking secrets or local-only instructions.
Customers can register, log in, log out, restore their session, and use protected features through secure JWT authentication.
Customers can search cities and stay dates, list qualifying hotels, inspect hotel details, and see available room types and starting prices.
Authenticated customers can idempotently reserve one available room unit with correct date, capacity, concurrency, and server-side price enforcement.
Customers can view only their own reservation details and statuses.
Administrators can manage hotels and rooms, view reservations, and update allowed statuses through protected APIs and UI.
PostgreSQL preserves the required relationships, constraints, history, and multi-unit inventory model.
The hotel details experience displays current city weather through an isolated backend integration that fails gracefully.
The Harbor Quiet design system produces responsive, accessible, consistent customer and administrator experiences.
Critical behavior is covered by machine-checkable unit, integration, concurrency, component, accessibility, and end-to-end tests.
The project is deployed to public frontend and API URLs with Neon persistence and verified production security configuration.
Professional documentation explains setup, architecture, APIs, security, reservation logic, deployment, and requirement coverage.
The user receives coherent Git checkpoints and exact PowerShell commands while retaining exclusive ownership of commits and pushes.
The user can explain the database, API, authentication, React data flow, errors, reservation logic, security boundaries, and deployment.

completeness_checklist.item: Goal restated in one concrete sentence
Scope boundary drawn with in-scope and out-of-scope work
Constraints and the 1.5-week calendar limit recorded
Every must requirement maps to at least one task
Every task has observable acceptance criteria and structured verification
Stop policy and human approval gate set

tasks.title: Establish the safe project foundation
tasks.description: Create the npm workspace, frontend and backend skeletons, committed ignore rules, safe environment example, health endpoints, formatting, linting, and verification scripts. Preserve local-only exclusions. After verification, provide the user exact PowerShell commands for the first commit and push.
acceptance_criteria: Frontend and backend start locally through documented npm commands.
The committed ignore file excludes credentials, build products, audit details, and local artifacts while allowing .env.example.
The assignment PDF, AGENTS.md, and local-workspace remain invisible to Git.
The origin URL equals the approved private GitHub repository, GitHub reports isPrivate true, and the agent has issued no commit or push operation.

tasks.title: Implement and approve the Harbor Quiet design foundation
tasks.description: Install the approved fonts, implement tokens and foundational components, then render representative customer and administrator screens at desktop and mobile widths before broader UI work.
acceptance_criteria: Color, typography, spacing, shape, buttons, forms, focus, statuses, and responsive layout match the approved design document.
A customer search surface and administrator table demonstrate the shared system at 320px and desktop widths.

The approved identity mark and favicon, flexible equal-height search controls, styled keyboard-accessible selects, room-dialog spacing, structured footer, and cookie-preference preview pass visual and interaction review.
The user approves screenshots before the remaining interface is built.

tasks.title: Build the PostgreSQL schema and migration system
tasks.description: Create versioned SQL migrations, database connection handling, constraints, indexes, active-record flags, reservation price snapshots and idempotency fields, deterministic development seed data, and a separate idempotent administrator provisioning command.
acceptance_criteria: A new database can be migrated and seeded from documented commands.
Required relationships and constraints reject invalid records.
Seed data contains no production credentials or reusable password, and administrator provisioning fails safely when explicit credentials are absent.
Database clients are released after successful and failed operations.

tasks.title: Implement authentication and authorization
tasks.description: Implement registration, login, logout, current-user restoration, Argon2id hashing, secure JWT cookies, current database role loading, strict custom-header, origin, and Fetch Metadata defenses, rate limits, and administrator authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Registration always creates a customer and never returns a password hash.
Production login emits a Set-Cookie header with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, and Path=/; logout expires the same cookie.
Unknown email and wrong password return the same public error.
Customer, missing-token, expired-token, missing-origin, invalid-origin, cross-site, missing-CSRF-header, and administrator cases are verified.
Only the current database role controls administrator access.

tasks.title: Implement hotel, room, search, and availability APIs
tasks.description: Implement administrator CRUD with historical-safe deactivation plus public browsing, search, details, room listing, capacity filtering, starting-price calculation, and informative availability results.
acceptance_criteria: All assignment hotel, room, and availability routes follow the documented contract.
Complete stay criteria return only hotels with qualifying remaining inventory.
Unauthorized changes, invalid values, and missing resources return stable errors.
Deactivated hotels and room types disappear from public results while historical reservations remain readable.
Starting price is computed from qualifying room types.

verifications.command: npm --workspace backend test -- hotels rooms availability

tasks.title: Implement the transaction-safe reservation engine
tasks.description: Implement idempotent confirmed reservation creation, customer ownership, administrator listing, confirmed-to-cancelled status updates, universal PostgreSQL inventory locking, overlap counting, inventory enforcement, and server-side nightly and total price snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Back-to-back stays are accepted while every true overlap shape is rejected when inventory is exhausted.
Multi-unit room types accept no more active overlapping reservations than total_rooms.
Two synchronized simultaneous attempts for the final unit create exactly one reservation.
Concurrent booking, cancellation, inventory-edit, and deactivation operations preserve valid inventory.
Repeating one reservation request with the same idempotency key creates exactly one reservation, while conflicting key reuse is rejected.
Nightly price and total price remain unchanged when the room type price changes later.
Clients cannot submit price, total, owner, role, or status.
A customer receives HTTP 404 for another customer's reservation, and only confirmed-to-cancelled is an allowed status transition.

verifications.command: npm --workspace backend test -- reservations concurrency pricing ownership

tasks.title: Build the customer application
tasks.description: Implement home search, hotel results, hotel details, authentication, reservation review, confirmation, My Reservations, structured footer navigation, guest-support links, and cookie preferences using relative API routes and server-authoritative data.
acceptance_criteria: The complete customer journey works through keyboard and pointer input.
URL state preserves search criteria between relevant pages.
Every asynchronous surface has loading, empty, failure, and success behavior, and stale responses cannot replace newer URL state.
The browser never calculates authoritative availability or price.
Footer links reach owner-reviewed privacy, reservation terms, accessibility, contact, and cookie-preference content without placeholder or broken destinations.
Non-essential scripts remain disabled until required consent is recorded, and the guest can reject or reopen preferences.

tasks.title: Build the administrator application
tasks.description: Implement protected administrator navigation, hotel forms, room forms, reservation listing, status filtering, status updates, destructive confirmations, and conflict recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Administrators can perform every assignment management action.
Customers cannot render or call administrator functionality.
Forms preserve server errors and prevent accidental duplicate submission.
Tables remain usable on mobile without hiding essential actions.

tasks.title: Integrate weather through the backend
tasks.description: Implement Open-Meteo geocoding and current-weather calls with validation, timeout, mapping, caching, and a non-blocking hotel-details presentation.
acceptance_criteria: The frontend never calls Open-Meteo directly.
Success returns only the documented internal weather shape.
Timeout, unknown city, malformed response, and upstream failure do not break hotel details.
Weather requests use bounded resources and a short cache.

tasks.title: Harden and audit the complete local application
tasks.description: Run formatting, linting, PostgreSQL-backed continuous integration, dependency, secret, accessibility, security, responsive, metadata, link, image-budget, failure-path, launch-readiness, and complete requirement audits. Resolve confirmed findings only after presenting the remediation plan.
acceptance_criteria: Every mandatory requirement has implementation and verification evidence.
No known high-confidence critical or high-severity finding remains unresolved.
No secret is detected in the working tree or Git history.
Desktop, 320px mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, targeted aria-live, and external-failure reviews pass.
Applicable launch-readiness checks have evidence, and every not-applicable check records a reason.
GitHub Actions passes against an ephemeral PostgreSQL service without requiring local Docker.

tasks.title: Deploy and verify the production system
tasks.description: Guide the user through Neon, Render, and Vercel configuration. Apply migrations, provision the administrator, configure secrets, rewrites, HTTPS headers, metadata, robots, and sitemap behavior, then run public health, customer, administrator, CSRF, consent, cookie-forwarding, cache, broken-link, and cold-start smoke checks.
acceptance_criteria: Public frontend and API URLs are reachable over HTTPS.
The frontend uses the production API rewrite, preserves every Set-Cookie security attribute, and rejects invalid mutation origins.
Neon persists data across API redeploys and cold starts.
Public pages have verified titles, descriptions, canonical and social metadata, intended indexability, a reachable sitemap, security headers, and no broken required links.
Production customer and administrator journeys pass without exposing secrets.

tasks.title: Finalize documentation and explanation readiness
tasks.description: Reconcile documentation with implemented evidence, complete local setup and API references, record public URLs, validate links and commands, record launch-readiness evidence and owner-reviewed guest policies, prepare the demonstration guide, and run the final assignment audit.
acceptance_criteria: The fresh-checkout verification script exits 0, the frontend root returns HTTP 200, and the API health route returns HTTP 200 with status ok.
Documentation describes only implemented and verified behavior.
Every mandatory assignment row links to evidence.
Privacy, reservation terms, accessibility, contact, and cookie-preference content is owner-reviewed, reachable, and dated before launch.
The user can walk through the ten required explanation topics using the demonstration guide.
